newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-PEN PICTURES OF WIMBLEDON WOMEN'S SEMIFINALISTS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PEN PICTURES OF WIMBLEDON WOMEN'S SEMIFINALISTS.

text.p: Pen pictures of the women's singles semifinalists at Wimbledon on Thursday:
MARTINA HINGIS (Switzerland) - WTA ranking 1. Wimbledon seeding 1. Age 16. Height 1.67 m. Weight 52 kg. Grand Slam victories: Australian Open (1997).

Became the youngest Grand Slam champion in the Open era when she won the Australian Open in January. Took over as world number one from Steffi Graf in March. Despite her low-key approach to the tournament after losing the French Open final to Iva Majoli, she has looked at home on the faster grass surface. Has not dropped a set in the tournament, averaging just 66 minutes on court in her five matches to date. Last year became youngest-ever Wimbledon champion when she won the women's doubles with Helena Sukova. Either herself or Kournikova will become the youngest Wimbledon finalist, beating the previous record held by Steffi Graf who reached the 1987 final at age 18. She has lost only one match this year -- to Majoli in the French Open. She prefers to stay at the baseline, relying on her consistent forehand and backhand. Czech-born but moved to Switzerland as a child. Named after Martina Navratilova by mother Melanie who is also her coach.
ANNA KOURNIKOVA (Russia) - WTA ranking 42. Unseeded. Age: 16. Height: 1.68m. Weight: 50kg. Grand Slam victories: None.

Making her debut at Wimbledon. She will rise at least 20 placings in the world rankings after reaching the semifinals in a women's tour event for the first time since making her professional debut in October 1995. Upset seventh seed Anke Huber and veteran Helena Sukova en route to the semis and recoverd from one-set down on three occasions to win. In her second round match against Barbara Rittner, valiantly fought back from 6-4, 5-1 down and two match points to win. Is striking the ball harder than any other female player in the tournament. Boasts a lethal whipping double-handed backhand. Moved to Florida with her mother Alla in 1992 to attend Nick Bollettieri's tennis school. In 1996 was named the most impressive newcomer on the women's tour. At age 14, became youngest player to compete and win in Fed Cup competition in the first tie of 1996, helping Russia defeat Sweden 3-0. Wears her long blonde hair in a single plait and her striking good looks have drawn a big following among photo journalists.
JANA NOVOTNA v ARANTXA SANCHEZ VICARIO
JANA NOVOTNA (Czech Republic) - WTA ranking 4. Seeding 3. Age 28. Height 1.75 m. Weight 63 kg. Grand Slam victories: None.

Runner-up here in 1993, she is assured of moving to number two in the world rankings after reaching the semifinals here. Her game is naturally suited to grass, but she has been inconsistent at the net this year and has been taken to three sets three times in the tournament. She suffered a knee injury in a doubles match, but showed now sign of the problem in beating Indonesia's Yayuk Basuki in straight sets in the quarter-finals. Said afterwards she was now suffering a sore arm. She beat Seles in Madrid Open final in May and reached the rained out final of the warmup tournament in Eastbourne. Has been a sentimental favourite at Wimbledon since she won hearts by sobbing on Duchess of Kent's shoulder after losing final to Steffi Graf when she had been within reach of victory.
ARANTXA SANCHEZ VICARIO (Spain) - WTA ranking 9. Seeding 8. Age 25. Height 1.69 m. Weight 56 kg. Grand Slam victories: French Open 1989, 1994. U.S. Open 1994.

Runner-up at Wimbledon for the past two years. She has not dropped a set in the tournament and has averaged even less court time than Hingis -- just 61 minutes. She was the first of a wave of Spanish baseliners to make their mark on world tennis, and whereas her countrymen have had their problems adapting to the faster grass surface, Sanchez has had no such worries. Her speed around the court, coupled with her powerful groundstrokes make her a superb allround player. Has won more than $11.6 million in her career. In 1995 became first Spanish player to hold the world number one ranking in the Open era. Won the 1989 French Open at age of 17 years six months -- a record at the time. Lost to Hingis in this year's French Open quarter-finals. Brothers Emilio and Javier played on the men's tour. Used to be Novotna's doubles partner but the pair have fallen out.
